notes: Publication-safe: no internal names, ids or paths.
Every figure with standin=true is a stand-in measured on a development model and will be re-measured on the release model; the standin and measured_on fields are draft markers only, not page copy.
Tone (user, 2026-10-30): confident, no hedging, no caveats, few insider details. Every claim on the page must be true exactly as worded.

model.name: [MODEL NAME]
model.one_line: A foundation model for experiment design: it reads a campaign's results so far and proposes which experiments to run next.

model_details.type: Pretrained foundation model for experiment design
model_details.inputs: The campaign so far: parameter settings and measured outcomes, plus declared outcome limits (a floor where runs fail, a ceiling where a readout saturates)
outputs: A full predictive distribution of the outcome at any untested setting
The probability that a run succeeds
Proposals for the next experiment or the next batch

training_data.summary: Pretrained entirely on about 10 million simulated optimisation campaigns. No real or customer data was used for training.
variation_in_training: Problems from one to a hundred parameters
Smooth landscapes, sharp optima, thresholds, step changes and regime switches
Noisy and replicated measurements, batch effects and hidden factors
Campaign histories collected by many different search strategies

intended_use: Choosing the next experiments in lab campaigns where each experiment is expensive: formulation, media and buffer optimisation, assay development, protocol and process parameters
Ranking a candidate list (for example a plate of untested formulations) by expected outcome and uncertainty
Campaigns that aim for a target value, stay within limits, or trade off several outcomes

operating_envelope.batch_proposals: one experiment to a full plate per round

model_card.evaluation_summary: Benchmark landscapes run through the same interface labs use, a public hyperparameter-optimisation benchmark (HPO-B) and a published cell-free protein expression campaign. None of them were seen in training.

headline_candidates.text_template: On benchmark landscapes with sharp optima and abrupt changes, it beats standard Bayesian optimisation in {wins} of {runs} campaigns.
It beats random search in {pct} of {runs} benchmark campaigns.
When it gives a 95% range, the result lands inside it {cov95} of the time. A standard Gaussian process: {gp_cov95}.
It finds half of the best 5% of formulations {factor}x faster than random screening.

benchmarks.title: Better results in fewer experiments
benchmarks.question: How close does each method get to the best possible result within 50 experiments?
benchmarks.task: Optimise benchmark landscapes the model never saw in training, 50 experiments in batches of 5.

dataset.citation: Surjanovic and Bingham, Virtual Library of Simulation Experiments

metric.name: Remaining gap to the optimum, relative to random search

paired.comparison: vs standard Bayesian optimisation, sharp optima and abrupt changes

benchmarks.title: Uncertainty you can trust
benchmarks.question: When the model gives an 80% or 95% range, how often does the measured value land inside?
benchmarks.task: Predict untested outcomes from campaign histories and check how often results land inside the predicted ranges.

metric.name: Share of results inside the 50% / 80% / 95% range

benchmarks.title: Public benchmark: HPO-B
benchmarks.question: How fast does each method find good configurations on a public benchmark it never saw?
benchmarks.task: Search real hyperparameter-optimisation spaces of up to 6 parameters, one experiment at a time.

dataset.name: HPO-B v3 test split
dataset.citation: Pineda Arango et al., NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks 2021

metric.name: Remaining gap to the best configuration after 25 and 50 experiments

benchmarks.title: Real lab data: cell-free protein expression
benchmarks.question: Given some measured formulations, which untested ones should be made next?
benchmarks.task: From a handful of measured formulations of a published three-stage campaign, pick which untested formulations to make next.

metric.name: Top-5% hit rate of its next picks; share of results inside its 80% range

200 measured formulations: results inside its 80% range

benchmarks.title: Experiments saved
benchmarks.question: How many fewer experiments to find the best formulations than random screening?
benchmarks.task: Search each cell-free stage for its top 5% / top 1% formulations, 200 experiments, one at a time.

metric.name: Acceleration factor: random's median experiments to the goal divided by the method's

capabilities.name: Batches
capabilities.text: Proposes a whole batch at once, from a single experiment to a full plate.

capabilities.name: Targets, not just maxima
capabilities.text: Aim for a value (for example 50% yield within a tolerance) and get the probability of landing in range.

capabilities.name: Failed runs and saturated readouts
capabilities.text: Declare where runs fail or a readout saturates; the model treats those outcomes as censored rather than exact.

capabilities.name: Limits on other outcomes
capabilities.text: Keep cost, purity or other measured outcomes within limits while optimising one.

capabilities.name: Several objectives
capabilities.text: Map the trade-off front between competing outcomes.

capabilities.name: Mixed parameter types
capabilities.text: Continuous, integer, log-scale, categorical parameters and mixtures that must sum to a total.

capabilities.name: No per-campaign tuning
capabilities.text: Nothing is fitted or tuned per campaign: the model reads the history and predicts directly.

enables.title: Every plate ranked, with honest uncertainty
enables.text: A team screening one plate a week gets the next plate proposed and every candidate ranked by expected outcome and by how sure the model is, so reagent goes to the wells that teach the most or are most likely to win.

enables.title: Failed runs count as information
enables.text: Campaigns where many conditions fail (precipitation, no growth, no signal) or a readout saturates can declare those limits instead of hiding or deleting the runs.

enables.title: Aim for a value, not just the maximum
enables.text: Hitting 50% yield within a tolerance, or a viscosity window, is a goal in its own right, with the probability of landing in range for every proposal.

enables.title: No modelling expertise per campaign
enables.text: There is no model to fit, kernel to choose or setting to tune: the lab supplies its results so far and gets the next experiments.

enables.title: From a few parameters to many
enables.text: The same model serves a two-factor optimisation and a formulation with dozens of components, mixing continuous, categorical and mixture parameters.
